claims.text: The initial material is polycrystalline (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy.
The untreated alloy has a homogeneous phase.
The untreated alloy is inherently brittle and cracks under mechanical stress.
An annealing temperature below the caloric transformation temperature can still be high enough to promote precipitation in this alloy.
The proposed annealing treatment will generate a fine-scale Fe–Co-rich phase at grain boundaries and within grains.
The annealing-induced Fe–Co-rich precipitates will be nanometer-scale and ductile.
The Fe–Co precipitates will form a crack-arresting network.
The precipitates will improve load transfer and provide compliant interfaces at grain boundaries.
The precipitates will arrest crack propagation and thereby improve compressive strength and durability.
The precipitates will not significantly interfere with the primary phase transformation responsible for the caloric effect.
Annealing will increase compressive strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The resulting strength may meet or exceed improvements achieved using epoxy- or In-containing composites.
The caloric temperature change under applied magnetic field or pressure will remain comparable to that of the untreated alloy.
The intervention is effective only within an optimized annealing temperature-and-duration window that avoids unwanted phase changes.
Unwanted annealing-induced phase changes could degrade the magnetocaloric or barocaloric response.
The proposed benefits are expected under magnetic-field, pressure-field, near-ambient thermal-cycling, and compressive-loading conditions.
